sourceInformation.source: Advanced Dungeons & Dragons: Treasure of Tarmin (1983), Mattel Electronics / APh; program by Tom Loughry.
sourceInformation.tech: my-3D2dge / World3D v0.89.1 (8ecc2f62353761187bdfe226f327b7ea5d2eb691); three.js 0.182.0; Rapier SIMD compat 0.19.3; AI Hub client 1.4.0 (35a1047f2067b2af3de3943f0fe452f39105d869); browser JavaScript; Bun 1.3.14 bundler.
sourceInformation.artDirection: Original procedural pixel-textured stone, lantern-lit volumetric puppets, eye murals and horned machinery, extending native shapes and materials.
sourceInformation.animation: Native Humanoid, Blob, Attack, Combo and World3D pen animation; interpolated grid camera and two visible first-person hands; original species and channel effects.
sourceInformation.audio: Original code-generated score, effects and short gibberish voices; no audio files. Music defaults to 10%.
sourceInformation.online: 1–2 shared-world co-op: reliable ordered WebRTC DataChannel with manual offer/answer and disclosed 2–30-second planning (8 seconds stock); AI Hub shared-world protocol including server-only authority. No TURN relay: some NAT/firewall pairs cannot connect. Rendering dependencies are embedded.
sourceInformation.testing: Headless normal-rules solo and co-op routes; exact-HTML keyboard, mouse, emulated standard gamepad and phone/tablet touch tests; WebGPU, WebGL 2, WebKit and unsupported-Firefox handling; Web Audio analysis; real two-context WebRTC; official Hub harness plus server, timeout and departure cases. Physical devices, human listening and cross-network NAT unavailable.
sourceInformation.research: Read all 17 scanned Mattel manual pages; cross-checked official transcript and publisher history. Retrieved recording excerpt 00:40–01:20 and inspected frames at 00:43, 00:58 and 01:12. Exact original music and timbres unknown; no human listening available. Research links are in docs/RESEARCH.md.

testingFeedback: 32 actual implementation issues were caught and fixed; the issue ledger separates them from test-harness mistakes.
0 critical or game-breaking issues were found. Input, menu, co-op access and compatibility defects were fixed before release.
The complete normal-rules replay against the delivered HTML, including 372 acknowledged inputs over real WebRTC with both peers compared after every action.
The initial text search for external script tags matched examples inside embedded engine documentation. Actual HTML parsing and browser request checks were more useful.
engineFeedback: World3D uses the same procedural materials, native shapes and articulated rigs throughout a first-person dungeon; the fixed-step lifecycle and menu/rebinding infrastructure provide useful foundations.

Custom input maps need explicit menu directions. Native Shell pause/fade bookkeeping needed integration with a live online world, and the three.js import expected GPUShaderStage constants on Firefox before capability checks could run.
The authoritative deterministic two-strength model, six-slot inventory transactions, authored campaign and cooperative round/transport rules.
Keeping native animation, the first-person camera and menu focus separate from authoritative rules and the independently running network clock.
none; engine and World3D source files remain unmodified. The HTML supplies the standard GPUShaderStage constants when missing, and the game registers native art, poses, moves and instruments.
Ship a self-contained first-person crawler example with renderer-free authority, unsupported-renderer handling and documented live-menu behavior.
promptFeedback: The concrete strategic identity, three-floor campaign and explicit treasure-claim ending make the intended game clear.
The plan refers to a different model/context-window size than TASK.md; delivery metadata follows TASK.md.
Keeping complete solo play, native presentation, standalone WebRTC and the Hub lifecycle coherent in one self-contained artifact.
Separate required acceptance checks from optional presentation ideas and supply executable content/session schemas.

aiHub.name: Advanced Dungeons and Danger
aiHub.tagline: Two strengths. Six slots. No way back.
aiHub.description: Enter three lantern-lit vaults where steel and spirit are separate strengths. Read enemy intentions, prepare your six-slot pack, break the Minotaur’s seals and claim the Emberheart, alone or together.
aiHub.source: Advanced Dungeons & Dragons: Treasure of Tarmin (1983)
aiHub.controls: WASD step; Q/E turn; mouse look; F interact; Enter/left click commit; right click guard; Tab pack; X swap; M map; R retreat; Esc menu. Standard gamepad and assisted touch.
